$about: Design decisions that depart from a rule on purpose, so nobody 'fixes' them by accident and everyone can see them (and reconsider them). Read by build/audit.mjs: an exception with an 'audit' entry is not reported as a failure, but it is measured and printed under 'Kept as designed' on every run, with the value of that run.
kind: exception = it fails a check (contrast, …) and is kept; decision = a deliberate choice the system's general rule does not make by itself.

audit.axe: the axe rule and the elements it may fail on (a regular expression on the target). audit.pixels: which texts drawn over a canvas this exception covers. The audit finds every text over a canvas by itself (axe cannot see a canvas) and measures it from the pixels behind it; one that fails and is not covered here is a failure.

decisions.what: CTA card: the white title and the white text sit on the purple card (#884dff) with white dust moving over it (15%, scripts/stipple.js; until Oct 19, 2026 on the light purple #b596ff between purple dots)
decisions.rule: WCAG 1.4.3 text contrast (3 : 1 large, 4.5 : 1 text), 1.4.11 focus indicator 3 : 1
decisions.measured: text 2.39 : 1, focus ring 1.93 : 1 (Oct 17, 2026, the old dots); with the white dust: the lead 4.4–4.5 : 1 at 320 px (the audit, Oct 19, 2026; the dust moves), the title passes
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-18 — kept for now
decisions.why: the look of the card: white dust over its text
decisions.fix: invClear in STIPPLE_CTA (the dust thins out round each text line: quietPad), or less dust (invOpacity); the focus ring can be ink on this card (8.8 : 1)

decisions.what: White text on the colours of the card stack and the stats: the orange «Документы» and green «Финансы» cards, their labels (also over the progress fill), the orange, green and blue stats
decisions.rule: WCAG 1.4.3 text contrast: the labels are 500, not bold, so they need 4.5 : 1
decisions.measured: labels on orange 2.95 (over the fill 2.17), on green 3.76 (2.52); stat labels 2.8 (orange) – 3.6 (green); stat numbers 2.3 (orange) – 2.8 (green) on the dots (Oct 17, 2026); since Oct 19, 2026 the stats are filled with their colour under white dust: «>20 000» and «Договоров» 2.95 on orange
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-17 (orange) and 2026-10-18 (green, the progress fill)
decisions.why: the brand colours of the subjects
decisions.fix: text-safe shades for text-bearing surfaces: orange #c25700, green #008a25 (4.5 : 1)

decisions.what: White text on the teal (Telegram-бот) and orange (FM Lens demo) buttons
decisions.why: the brand colours of the two tools

decisions.what: The grey notes of the footer (ink 50% on the footer grey)
decisions.why: a quiet legal line

decisions.what: Tool cards are padded by their own width (--tool-pad: 28px on a 288px card, about 40 on a 384px one, 64 from a 600px card), above their radius (radius/l, 32 → 56) on every card wider than about 330px; every other card is padded by its radius. Under the text, above the picture, at least --pad-l (40 → 64)
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-18 (the air); the padding by the card's width on 2026-10-18 (28–32 on a 320 phone, 40 on a 420 one)
decisions.why: extra air on a big two-column card with a picture, without a narrow column of text on a phone

decisions.what: Where two lines of the hero title do not fit (about under 430px), it takes three: «Весь лейбл. / На одной / волне». Chosen by fit (a container query in the title's em), not by a screen width
decisions.why: keeps the hero a size above the section headings on phones (36 vs 28px at 320)

decisions.what: The logo strip shows whole columns (2, 3, 4, chosen by its own width). Adding a column makes the tiles smaller at once (−33% from 2 to 3, −25% from 3 to 4); the steps are the shared steps S and M, where the features above change too (tiles ≥ 112 and ≥ 164px)
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-18 (whole columns; 3 columns down to a 390 screen, in step with the features)
decisions.why: whole columns preferred over a fluid tile with a partly shown column

decisions.what: The ID cards are an object of a fixed size (240 × 345px), scaled as a whole by the row or the deck, corners included: 24px of the card's 240 (the table half that in), so the card keeps its shape at every screen size. Their deck starts below a 35rem column, their own step: the row needs that room
decisions.decided: 2026-10-18; radius/m on 2026-10-18 (Tim); 16px, scaled with the card, on 2026-10-20 (Tim: smaller corners, always in proportion to the card); 24px on 2026-10-22 (Tim: 24 at most)
decisions.why: their text stays readable at one size; a card is one object, so its corners belong to it, not to the screen

decisions.what: Running text is 16px at every screen width (type/body); short text in small cards (the features, the bylines) is type/body-s, 14 → 16; the text of the tool cards type/body-m, 16 → 18
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-18; body-s and body-m on 2026-10-18
decisions.why: readable text on phones, and room in the small tiles (two features in a row down to a 390 screen)

decisions.what: Every text size ends on the ladder (steps of 2 up to 24, 4 up to 64, 8 up to 128) at 320 and 1440: hero 36 → 60 (60 at most: Tim, 2026-10-22), h2 28 → 52 (also the stack card titles), card-heading 24 → 32, lead 16 → 20, card-tag 14 → 18, body-m 16 → 18, body 16, body-s 14 → 16, ui 14. No modular ratio any more: the levels keep their order and distance by type.relations (at least ×1.125 apart at both ends), checked by build/tokens.mjs
decisions.why: round end values, sizes chosen by eye (hero 60–64 on a computer, lead 20, h2 = card title)
decisions.costs: lead = body on phones (16), body-m = body = 16 and body-s = ui = 14 on phones

decisions.what: Blocks change their layout together, at three shared column widths: S 22rem (a 390 screen: features 1 → 2, logos 2 → 3), M 43rem (a 768 window, also with a classic scrollbar: logos 3 → 4; royalty, publications, tools 1 → 2), L 58rem (a 1024 window, also with a scrollbar: features 2 → 4). The ID cards' deck is the one exception (35rem)
decisions.why: things on the page change at the same moments, not each at its own width

decisions.what: The royalty cards fill their column and arrange themselves by their own shape: narrow — the drawing on top, the title from 70% of the card's width; wide (from a 32rem card) — the title left, the drawing right. Titles as wide as the card, at most 14em (three lines, never two long ones; 12em and evened-out lines until 2026-10-22, Tim: full width)
decisions.why: no title over the drawing at any width (it was, between 621 and 890px), no capped card on a phone

decisions.what: A stack card is laid out vertically (text on top, the drawing below) when it is less than 1.3 times as wide as tall, and on every screen about 1440px tall or taller (a card 83rem tall), whatever its width; the drawing grows up to 1080px with its room
decisions.why: on a tall monitor the horizontal card left a small drawing in a lot of air

decisions.what: Things that move by themselves without end and have no pause switch: the CTA's strip of words, the hero chips, the ring's idle spin, the dust of the stats and the CTA, the loops in the drawings. They all stop for visitors who turned on "reduce motion"
decisions.rule: WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (moving content that lasts more than 5 seconds can be paused)
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-18 — no pause switch, the strip keeps its loop
decisions.why: the look of the page; reduce motion covers the visitors who need it
decisions.fix: a site-wide pause switch (remembered), or the strip moved by the scroll

decisions.what: The burger menu's pills open with the settle curve, from 20% to 117% and back to 100%, 0.8s in all, and close by playing the same backwards
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-18 — kept as designed
decisions.why: the character of the menu

decisions.what: The cookie notice is the same card at every screen width (276px, fixed radii 16/8, 12px text: type/note), not fluid like the rest of the page; its text uses ink 70%, its button black 5% (7% under the mouse: --tint-strong); its links underlined 1px, 3px under the baseline, in ink 20% (Tim, Oct 19; Figma has 10%), ink 30% under the mouse, as in Figma; its line height is the site's text one (1.3) instead of Figma's 1.25; after «ОК» the text stays, «ОК» turns into a drawn checkmark, the card sets off 0.15 s before the drawing ends and goes down below the screen edge while fading (0.45 s, the 'leave' curve of motion.js, as the stack titles leave)
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-19 — the Figma section 'cookies'; the exit (text stays, card goes down with an existing curve) on his request
decisions.why: a small note in the corner that should look the same everywhere; 1.3 is the line height of all small text on the site

decisions.what: Only «ОК» counts as consent: nothing optional (analytics, a chat) starts before it (scripts/consent.js, onConsent). The answer is kept 12 months on the device, with the version of the text (VERSION); a visitor who has not answered is asked again on the next visit
decisions.decided: Claude, 2026-10-19 — proposed to Tim with the cookie notice
decisions.why: 152-ФЗ art. 9: consent is specific and unambiguous; by 2026 practice, staying on the page or scrolling is not treated as consent to analytics
decisions.fix: if the text keeps «Оставаясь, вы даете согласие», it promises more than the code does: change it to «Нажимая «ОК», вы даёте согласие…», or accept that analytics waits for «ОК» anyway

decisions.what: In Safari 26+ on a Mac the page scrolls in its own box (.page, position fixed, inset 0) instead of the window; everywhere else the window scrolls as before. boot.js gives <html> the class boxed; scroller.js is what every script asks about scrolling; GSAP's ScrollTrigger watches the box (gsap.js), and the logos are held there by position: sticky instead of GSAP's pin. ?fmbox=1 / ?fmbox=0 force it on or off
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-19 — wanted a solid Safari bar, as on YouTube and Google Docs
decisions.why: Safari 26+ on a Mac draws its bar as glass over the page and the page shows through while it scrolls. Measured in Tim's Safari on macOS 27: no light header (solid, glass, tone strips) made the bar solid in dark mode; a page whose window does not scroll did, in light and dark mode (the Google Docs way). theme-color is ignored. Checked in Chromium: the boxed page renders pixel for pixel like the normal one at 1440×900, 390×844 and 1366×650

decisions.what: The privacy policy and the cookie consent are pages of the site (privacy_policy_ru.html, soglasie_cookie.html) at their old addresses. Their text is the Tilda text as it was (Tim, 2026-10-19: «keep it as is for now except formatting»); only the layout is new: headings, paragraphs, hanging list markers, one card per purpose of processing, links. Text line height 1.5 (--doc-line), not --lh-text 1.3
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-19 (text as is); Claude, 2026-10-19 (layout, line height)
decisions.why: a long legal text is read line after line; 1.3 suits the page's short texts. The wording waits for a separate review (errors listed in the chat of Oct 19)
decisions.fix: when the text is revised, edit it in the two pages directly

decisions.what: The hero has least and greatest sizes for its parts (picture, air above and below the text). On tall screens it stops growing and the first card shows more under it (390×844: 574px instead of 826); on screens shorter than about 690px it is taller than the screen rather than squeezing the picture (1366×650: 673px, the team 291px tall instead of 249, no pill of the first card on the first screen)
decisions.decided: Claude, 2026-10-19, from Tim's round-4 comments (hero 1–3) — to confirm
decisions.why: the hero should neither stretch nor shrink too much; generous air round the text; a big enough team at ≈620px tall
decisions.fix if reconsidered: lower hero/pic-min or hero/air-top/bottom in design/scale.json to bring the first card's pill back on short laptops

decisions.what: A card that has become a pill does not wait: it goes on up with the page at once and leaves the screen under the navbar, while the next card comes up to the top. The pinned pill of 2026-10-19 is gone, and its code with it (the sticky holder round each card, the last card's copy, SET.hold)
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — remove the sticky behaviour of a closed card pill (it was pinned for 1/5 of a screen since 2026-10-19, round-4 comment cards 5); the same day — remove the pause from the code completely
decisions.why: the pause felt like the page sticking; without it the stack scrolls on evenly
decisions.fix if reconsidered: bring back the holder of PR #13 (git history: stack.css .stack__hold, cards.js SET.hold and endPin)

decisions.what: The publications show at most 4 cards; with 5 or more, a «Показать больше» pill under them shows the next 4 each time and goes away when none are left. It is --section-gap below the cards (the gap their heading had; Tim, 2026-10-20), while the heading itself has --section-air-l above the cards. It is a line button (.btn--line): no colour of its own, a 1px border, ink 70% on an ink 16% border, ink on ink 25% under the mouse (Tim, 2026-10-20), and it comes in as a block, as the hero's button does. Without scripts every card is shown and the button is not
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — button below the cards from 5 cards; later the same day: no background, 1px border, 70%/16% → 100%/25%, coming in like the hero's button
decisions.why: the list can grow without the page getting longer; 4 is two full rows of the two-column grid
decisions.fix if reconsidered: PUBS in scripts/pubs.js (first, more); the colours in sections.css (.pubs__more)

decisions.what: No focus ring anywhere on the page (links, buttons, the publications the focus moves to after «Показать больше», the booking window's close button). Only the system's high-contrast modes (forced colours) keep a ring, in the system's colour. The skip link still appears when it is reached with Tab
decisions.rule: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (and 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured relies on seeing the focus)
decisions.measured: outline none on every focused element (Oct 20, 2026: a publication after «Показать больше», a footer link after Tab)
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — remove all design for focus states
decisions.why: the purple ring showed on the publication the focus moves to after «Показать больше», and on other elements; the look of the page
decisions.fix: base.css: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--purple); outline-offset: 3px } (the ring before Oct 20), or a quieter one (ink 30%, 2px)

decisions.what: The tools and the publications have more air than the other sections: --section-air-l (56 → 112px) above and below their content and from their headings to their cards, the same as under the CTA card (which had section-y × 1.4, the same numbers). The gap from the publications to «Показать больше» stays --section-gap
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-20 — top and bottom paddings 112 at most (as under the CTA card), the heading gap 112 too, the button's gap unchanged
decisions.why: the two sections after the CTA read as a calmer, more spacious end of the page

decisions.what: Safari's bottom bar on iPhone takes no colour from the page: an empty block fixed over the middle of the bottom edge (.bar-guard, base.css; iOS only, 64 × 8px, takes taps), which Safari skips as see-through and then finds nothing fixed or sticky there, so the bar stays plain glass. Before, the bar turned the colour of the stack's cards and kept it after the stack (WebKit hit-tests the bottom edge through clipping and through blocks with nothing sticky in them, so the last card hidden by the stack's overflow still counted). A backdrop filter on the block (Oct 22) made the bar white instead
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-22 — «i don't want it to have any color», then «i want it to have no background» (white was not it either)
decisions.why: the green of «Финансы» stayed in the bar over the sections after the stack. WebKit LocalFrameView::fixedContainerEdges: the bar is coloured only when the hit test at the bottom edge finds a fixed or sticky container; a see-through fixed block that takes taps ends that search with nothing; a backdrop filter counts as glass of many colours (Safari then paints the bar the page colour, white)

decisions.what: Known limit, left as it is: in Telegram's browser on iPhone, a hard fling past the end of the page makes the strip behind Telegram's buttons (the white cap, nav.js initCap) flicker for 3–5 frames (about 50–80 ms). Everywhere else the cap holds at the navbar (±1px, measured frame by frame in Tim's recordings with ?fmcap=debug, Oct 23)
decisions.decided: Tim, 2026-10-23 — «let's do this» (record it and leave it): the top bar is white in general, a split-second flicker on a hard scroll past the end
decisions.why: the flicker is Telegram's own: in those frames it animates its top bar and moves the whole page, the fixed navbar too (debug: nav top −72, visual viewport +72); the page hears of it only after those frames are drawn, and the browser of Telegram has no setting to keep its bar still (Mini Apps have one, ordinary links do not). Already done: the bounce off in the last screen, the cap placed by the navbar's offsetTop, its scroll-driven animation 1:1 with the scroll (animation-range), its place checked 4 times a second
decisions.fix: none from the page; look again if Telegram changes its browser (test with ?fmcap=debug: the cap turns red)
